title: Reading evidence — the value of pkit::documentation:reading-evidence, version 1
description: The data point's companion schema (COR-052 point 5; living-docs DEC-001 point 7): the results of executed checks that follow the documentation — a simulated reader running a guide against the system, say. This capability runs no such check; the results arrive from a capability that does, or from the project's own filler file. One entry per page or path and commit, keyed by the pair: its `id` is `<path>@<commit>`. The point is `union`, no default takes part, and its inert policy is `fallback`, because the evidence advises: it informs a reader-review and never replaces one (DEC-001 point 6). The version rises only on a change that breaks existing fillers.

commit.description: A commit, by its full or abbreviated hexadecimal name.

evidence.description: The result of one executed check, for one page or path at one commit.

id.description: The entry's key, the pair it is for: `<path>@<commit>`.

path.description: What the check followed: a page, by its repository-relative path, or a reader path through several pages, by a gitignore-style pattern matching them.

commit.description: The commit the check ran against.

outcome.description: `passed`: the reader could follow it. `failed`: they could not.

description.description: One line a person reads: what was checked, and what was found.
